subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@aurorafinance.com>, Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Hi Alice/Bryan 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Please let me know if I've missed anything.

1) Primary pains you shared
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak hours when using multi-tenant endpoints (spikes impacting customer SLAs).
- Data isolation and compliance requirements for financial PII (need dedicated instances to ensure separation and auditability).
- Cost uncertainty: current spend varies by month and makes forecasting/ops planning difficult.

2) Current stack
- Inference today: in-house app calls third-party hosted LLM endpoints for summarization and KYC workflows.
- Traffic profile: bursty daily peaks (8am-10am ET and 2pm-4pm ET), average 120 TPS at peak, 20k tokens/minute during peak bursts.
- Authentication and logs: central logging in Splunk, secrets in AWS Secrets Manager.

3) Success criteria for Dedicated fit
- Predictable 95th percentile latency <= 150ms for single-turn requests at 120 TPS sustained.
- Reserved capacity and network isolation (VPC) with SOC2 audit logs available to Aurora.
- Autoscale/burst behavior: ability to handle 2x peak bursts for up to 10 minutes with graceful degradation beyond that.
- Clear unit economics: target effective cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll refine after PoC).

4) Proposed PoC scope (what we agreed on)
- 2-week PoC on Redwood Dedicated: reserved pool sized for your steady-state (~120 TPS) with burst capacity to 240 TPS.
- Integrate with your VPC & KMS; ship logs to your Splunk instance.
- Run two workload profiles: latency-sensitive single-turn inference and batched summarization jobs.
- Measure: P95 latency, error rates, cost per token, and autoscale trigger behavior.

5) Next steps / owners
- Redwood: send SOW draft + capacity worksheet and pricing (Marissa)  Done (attached draft & spreadsheet).
- Aurora infra: share firewall/VPC contact and preferred test cluster region (Alice).
- Schedule kickoff: propose Wed 24 Jun for environment setup + baseline run (Bryan/Marissa).

6) Open questions we flagged
- Burst tolerance: confirm whether 2x for 10 minutes is sufficient vs. 3x for 5 minutes.
- Legal: any template changes required for PoC data handling (we can use a short-term data processing addendum).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sow-draft.pdf (SOW + pricing outline), aurora-capacity-template.xlsx (capacity inputs we used in the call).

Thanks  happy to jump back on a quick call if you want to tighten any of the acceptance criteria.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alice Kim <alice.kim@aurorafinance.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Thanks Marissa  this looks great and captures what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Our "120 TPS at peak" number is per-service (we have two services that will drive load). For the PoC please size to cover both services combined so assume 240 TPS steady-state, with a 2x burst target to 480 TPS for short spikes.
- Latency SLA: 150ms P95 sounds reasonable for single-turn, but for batched summarization jobs we care more about throughput and cost  conservative on latency there.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required; we also need an exportable audit trail for 12 months.

Quick Q on the SOW: can you include a short section describing rollback/fallback behavior if Dedicated experiences capacity constraints? We want to know what the fail-open/fail-closed behavior looks like.

Happy to kick off Wed 24 Jun  Bryan will send availability.

Thanks,
Alice
Director of Platform Engineering
Aurora Finance

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Kim <alice.kim@aurorafinance.com>, Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@aurorafinance.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Alice  thanks for the clarifications, very helpful. Updated recap below and plan of record: 

- PoC sizing: Redwood will size the reserved pool for 240 TPS steady-state (both services combined) with burst capacity to 480 TPS for short periods. We'll instrument and validate autoscale triggers and measurable fallbacks.
- Latency: P95 target 150ms for single-turn requests; batched summarization jobs measured for throughput/cost tradeoffs.
- Compliance: SOC2 + 12-month exportable audit logs supported; we'll include the export mechanism in the SOW appendix.
- Rollback/fallback behavior: Redwood Dedicated will expose routing policies  during capacity constraints we can route non-critical traffic to a lower-cost multi-tenant variant (configurable, can be disabled). We'll add explicit runbook steps and circuit-breaker behavior to the SOW appendix as you requested.

Next actions (updated owners):
- Marissa: produce updated SOW with explicit rollback/runbook section and final pricing for the 240->480 TPS PoC (attached updated SOW).
- Rafael (SE): prepare runbook and test plan for autoscale/burst and smoke tests. Rafael  can you share a brief test checklist by EOD today?
- Alice/Bryan: confirm kickoff date/time and share VPC/firewall contact.

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-sow-draft.pdf (v2 with rollback/runbook appendix), aurora-capacity-template.xlsx (we updated the steady-state/burst fields per your note).

Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Kim <alice.kim@aurorafinance.com>, Bryan Lee <br yan.lee@aurorafinance.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - Aurora Finance

Quick checklist for PoC (high-level):

1) Environment prep (Day 0)
- Confirm VPC peering & firewall rules (ports: 443 for control plane, SSH for debug if agreed).
- KMS integration test account + service principal for key rotation test.

2) Baseline validation (Day 1)
- Smoke test: single-turn request P95 baseline and error-rate check.
- Verify log export to Aurora Splunk instance (verify fields and retention).

3) Load profile tests (Day 2-5)
- Sustained run at 240 TPS for 30 minutes, measure P95/P99, CPU/GPU utilization.
- Burst run: ramp to 480 TPS for 10 minutes, validate autoscale triggers and any queued requests.

4) Failure modes & fallback (Day 6)
- Simulate node loss and observe routing to fallback model/variant.
- Validate circuit-breaker triggers and alerting.

5) Reporting & handover (Day 7-10)
- Deliver metrics report: latency percentiles, cost per 1k tokens, autoscale events, and logs export verification.

I'll produce a detailed checklist and a small test harness snippet for your infra team by end of day.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
